args.name: Evidence-based preservation of roots or berries
args.function: Provide a learnable way to test preservation of known-safe roots or berries, with explicit material costs, processing conditions, and observable spoilage outcomes. The problem is keeping a finite gathered food reserve usable longer, not merely labeling it preserved.
args.conditions: Sol has five gathered roots at tick 10. Root nutrition is known as 14 and toxicity as zero; berry nutrition is 8 and toxicity zero. The local root source currently has zero stock. The available cultivation interface explicitly has no root propagation, growth, harvest, or replenishment rule. Sol has no assumed tools, fire, containers, preservation equipment, or preservation mastery.
args.inputs: A small quantity of owned roots or berries for a controlled trial; any required equipment, fuel, workspace, or other materials must be specified and obtained rather than assumed.
args.costs: Unknown learning time, work, ingredients, processing duration, and losses. Specify these and cancellation behavior before committing food or starting persistent work.
args.effects: Enable an actual preservation trial, if feasible, with inspectable processing state and evidence of food retained or lost. Any change to spoilage, nutrition, or safety must result from the implemented physical process. A request, label, or completed lesson alone must not preserve food or establish safety.

candidates.costs: A game round to begin study after review; implementation time does not advance simulation.

candidates.function: Plant one owned root unit in a small soil plot as a persistent trial, inspect a plot by direct observation, or take back remaining planted material; resume or cancel unfinished planting.
candidates.costs: Plant: one owned unspoiled root unit (quantity 1); two work rounds at one energy each, at an unoccupied ordinary-soil x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; supply inputStackId. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: one round and 0.2 energy, the baseline probe observation of a plot in reach (target). Remove: one round and 1 energy, planter only (target). Tend is unavailable and spends nothing. No tools or water are granted.
candidates.effects: Completed planting places the real root unit in the plot; it keeps ageing under existing environmental decay while the planter is absent. Plot state records stage, observation rounds, soil moisture and temperature/rain exposure. There is no propagation, growth, harvest or replenishment rule for roots, so a plot never produces food. Inspect records only visible state. Remove returns only the material that physically remains, never a replacement; the emptied plot remains. Cancel releases unplanted material once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward for planting, inspecting or removing; genuine observed changes use the existing evidence-deduplicated probe feedback only.

response.text: {"queries":[],"result_json":"{\"reviews\":[{\"actor\":\"sol\",\"decision\":\"develop\",\"ability\":null,\"reason\":\"Develop a general controlled food-processing trial with passive air-drying and untreated-control modes. The supplied searches and available registry descriptions identify gathering, eating, observation and cultivation, but no demonstrated equivalent preservation function. Cultivate-plant explicitly leaves food ageing without preservation or replenishment; eating and gathering cannot substitute. Retrieval is incomplete and no query batches remain: the current-conversation development handoff must check remaining registered handlers for functional coverage and reuse applicable code rather than claim reinvention. Passive drying of whole known-safe food is a feasible experiment, not a guarantee of successful preservation. Do not invent tools, fire, clean containers, suitable weather or drying mastery.\",\"specification\":\"General operation: controlled-food-processing-trial, parameterized by mode (start, inspect, resume, cancel, retrieve), owned food stack references, quantity, treatment (initially whole-food passive air-drying), workspace coordinates and processId. Applicable actors study separately. Initial executable protocol uses one whole unit as treatment and one whole unit of the same resource and comparable existing age/decay as an untreated comparison; maximum initial batch is two food units. No cutting, heating, salting, fermentation or sealed storage is implied. A one-unit exposure trial may be allowed when only one unit is available, but must report the absence of a matched control and cannot establish comparative extension of usability.\\nExact current references: Sol owns item-4-sol-17, root quantity 5, quantityTenths 50, harvestedAt 4, recorded decay 6.98365183. Root nutrition 14 and toxicity 0 are known starting properties, not evidence that future spoiled roots remain safe. Berry nutrition 8 and toxicity 0 are known, but Sol owns no supplied berry stack. start-2-roots has stock 0 and supplies nothing; cultivate-plant cannot replenish it. start-2-berries, start-2-branches and forest-bark-2 are observed possible sources, not inventory grants. Existing gather transfers finite source stock at 2 energy per unit after actual travel into interaction range. Existing navigate, gather, probe, eat, pickup and drop handlers must be reused where applicable, with their references and revisions recorded in the implementation manifest; preserve foundation-forest@1 attribution where supplied.\\nPrerequisites and material costs: two owned unspoiled units of known-safe food, two owned intact bark pieces, two owned branches, and an accessible stable workspace with two separate positions. The proposed minimal support is two unsealed bark surfaces supported above soil by the branches, with no bindings, cutting or assumed tools. Implementation must validate actual material geometry, stability, food contact suitability and cleanliness from physical state. Bark is not automatically sanitary. If these checks cannot be implemented for available materials, do not consume food or fabricate a rack: return the unmet physical prerequisite and admit the necessary support preparation/contact-safety mechanism into this same development handoff. Materials must first be obtained; acquiring two branches and two bark pieces with gather costs 8 energy plus travel and elapsed rounds, subject to real stock and applicability. Materials remain real recoverable objects rather than being converted into free equipment.\\nLearning: 3 simulation rounds after implementation, with normal metabolism and no granted mastery before completion. Setup: two work rounds at 1 energy each to place and validate supports, followed by two work rounds at 1 energy each to allocate and place treatment and comparison food. Total setup is four work rounds and 4 energy, excluding acquisition, travel and learning. Validate and disclose the full plan before committing food. Reserve exactly the selected units, preserving origin, age, decay and all existing state; never reset freshness on splitting or transfer. For Sol, a two-root trial leaves three roots outside the experiment, each continuing ordinary ageing. Treatment and comparison use distinct positions under the same ambient conditions; expose the treatment on a validated raised, ventilated surface and leave the comparison under the existing ordinary ground-storage conditions. Record this difference explicitly; it tests the complete exposure/storage treatment, not drying alone. No perfectly matched environment or scientific certainty is fabricated.\\nProcessing dependency: implement or reuse a versioned per-resource food-state model before enabling any changed shelf life. It must account for initial dry matter and water, elapsed simulation time, measured ambient temperature, moisture or humidity, ventilation, rain/wetting, contact contamination and spoilage. The current packet supplies no drying coefficients, validated safe moisture threshold or complete spoilage model. Obtain these from implementation facts if present; otherwise develop the missing moisture/spoilage mechanism in this handoff and disclose its numeric rates, units, supported resource profiles, safe-use criteria and maximum observation horizon before execution. Do not silently invent calibrated constants or reinterpret the existing decay number as moisture. Whole roots or berries may dry too slowly, rewet, contaminate or spoil before useful drying. If no defensible resource-specific drying model is available yet, enable only the paired exposure-and-observation precursor: both samples retain existing decay rules, and no preserved status, safety certification or extended lifetime is awarded. This precursor is an actual finite-material experiment, not a roadmap or an unlock gated by an arbitrary era.\\nOngoing work: after setup, exposure runs each actual simulation round until cancellation, retrieval, spoilage exhaustion or a predeclared endpoint of 10 exposure rounds. Ten rounds is an observation checkpoint, not a promised processing duration or preservation threshold. No active energy is charged merely for passive exposure; elapsed time and metabolism still occur. Inspection is one round and 0.2 energy at the existing observation interface's reachable distance, reusing its handler where supported. Work requires the operator within reach; leaving or interruption pauses unfinished manual work at its completed round boundary without duplicating costs. Passive exposure, decay, rain and contamination continue while unattended. Rain or unsuitable conditions can defeat the treatment; protection, cleaning, turning and repairs are not automatic. Any extra action needs a disclosed implemented cost and real material prerequisites.\\nConservation and effects: food dry matter and any existing nutritional content are conserved except documented physical losses or spoilage; water leaving food enters the environment, and wetting transfers actual environmental water under the implemented model. Drying cannot multiply root nutrition 14 or berry nutrition 8, make new servings, remove toxins by declaration or reset age. Nutrition is applied by the existing eat handler only to actually consumed remaining edible material, with appropriate fractional accounting if the engine supports it; otherwise preserve whole-unit accounting without rounding gains. Spoiled matter remains identified waste unless a real removal process exists. Supports suffer only implemented wear/contamination and require actual repair or replacement if damaged. Outputs are surviving treatment food, surviving comparison food, any actual spoiled matter, the placed supports and a provenance-linked observation record. Successful preservation requires the implemented physical state and observed evidence; absence of visible mould alone cannot certify safety. No roots grow or sources refill.\\nInterruption and settlement: setup progress and payments persist by processId. Cancel or failed validation releases only surviving reserved food and unused materials exactly once; already placed supports remain in place. Retrieve costs one work round and 1 energy per food batch, checks reach and ownership, and transfers only actual remaining contents. Cancel after placement stops further scheduled work, not natural ageing or weather exposure, and does not teleport food to inventory. Completed work, consumed energy, elapsed time, moisture loss and spoilage are never refunded. Death releases reserved items locally according to existing death handling, leaves placed objects and samples in the world, and does not restore spoiled food. Passive environmental processes continue independently. Global review/development waiting advances no time; simulation pauses freeze all progress and environmental updates. Implement validation, rates, reservations, ownership, progress, settlements and deduplication in code rather than sending established rules back for repeated model judgment.\",\"learning\":3,\"experienceReview\":\"No pleasure, satisfaction, nutrition or skill reward for requesting, registration, learning, reserving food, issuing an inspection query or naming a product preserved. Only an actually performed observation yielding verified new information—including documented failure—may enter the existing evidence-deduplicated probe feedback. Require actor-local evidence and personal applicability, and key deduplication by material lineage, treatment, measured change and observation interval so inspecting through multiple interfaces cannot farm the same fact. Use existing coded feedback caps, amount, decay and cooldown; if those are not established, grant no new experience increment until a bounded policy is implemented. Familiar legitimate practice can qualify under an existing modest maintained-benefit policy without compulsory novelty, but not on passive timer completion alone. No extra mood path is introduced. Physical comfort remains capped at 10; food nutrition is never reduced by mood. Protected reward accounts, budget, goals and permissions remain untouched. Other actors must independently communicate and perform any participation; no consent or assistance is assumed.\",\"visualReview\":\"Emit real events for material reservation, completed setup steps, exposure start, measured drying or wetting, visible spoilage, inspection, interruption, resumption, cancellation and retrieval. Reusable visual metadata should include processId, resource, source item lineage, treatment/control role, position, quantities, work completed/required, timestamp, observed condition, evidence reference and status such as preparing, exposed, interrupted, spoiled, retrieved or inconclusive. Only render moisture values or contamination details that the observing actor can actually measure; internal model state is not automatically visible. Show actual bark supports and distinguish the samples without claiming that a label changes food. A completed lesson or elapsed timer cannot display preserved/safe/success. If validated evidence supports longer usability, show the specific measured comparison and limitations rather than universal safety. Failed or incomplete setup remains visibly failed or incomplete, and no inspection reveals hidden resources or unknown stock.\"}]}"}
